notes: All 7 searches ran; none was refused. The site search found Tran's office hosting a copy of the 15 September 2026 letter to Speaker Johnson asking the House to stay in session on AI risks; that is one of the centrally handled multi-signer letters, so it is left out here as instructed. Other AI-adjacent items seen in search summaries but not his own statements on AI risk: an FY27 community project funding request for a CSU Fullerton workforce hub that includes training AI practitioners, a 2025 Congressional App Challenge announcement, and a reported vote for the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) on data center grid costs (not verified at source). No source shows him sponsoring or co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538); the congress.gov cosponsor page returned HTTP 403 and could not be checked directly, and search results gave conflicting cosponsor lists that did not include him. Opened tran.house.gov press releases (page 1 of 25, 12 Nov to 30 Sep 2026) and In the News (page 1): no AI items. Older press release pages were not opened, so earlier AI remarks on his site could have been missed. Search results for the risk-topic queries mostly returned unrelated people (for example a 'Vu Tran' formerly at Meta), not this representative.
